newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil holds at new low level.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil holds at new low level.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps held steady at midday on Wednesday as the market found a new support level after big losses early this week, brokers said.
"The market is a bit shaky as China is not buying but there is some support at the lower level," one trader said.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $28.90/$29.05 a barrel, against Tuesday's $28.80/$28.90. The market traded in the morning at between $28.78 and $28.92 a barrel, brokers said.
Brokers estimated that between 200,000 and 300,000 barrels were traded in the morning.
The February/March time spread narrowed to 25/35 cents from last weeks 70/80 cents, reflecting the fundamental weakness of the prompt market, traders said.
Prices collapsed by over $3 a barrel within the week on big losses in crude and product prices in the West as well as poor regional demand.
The market remains weak as prices in the West have not recovered with the February Brent closing down 12 cents to $23.36 a barrel on Tuesday.
February IPE gas oil also closed weaker, down $5.25 to $213.75 a tonne on Tuesday.
Traders said refiners in Singapore, South Korea, Thailand and even Taiwan are offering gas oil cargoes for export.
Fuel oil edged down slightly with February was last quoted at $113.25/$114.50 per tonne, from Tuesday's $113.50/$114.00, brokers said.
